display.purpose: The homepage masthead and note titles. The largest serif on the page.

headline.purpose: Section titles and the contact band heading.

body.purpose: Long-form note copy, capped at 70 characters by --col-text.

ui.purpose: Nav links, buttons and form controls. Sans only.

meta.purpose: Department labels, dates, read times, chart axis values. Mono only.

shadows.name: ambient-popover
shadows.purpose: Under the notes dropdown and mobile menu. Signals floating above the page.

shadows.name: menu
shadows.purpose: The curve card's maturity menu. Tighter, because it drops from a control.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Note rows and Right now cards on hover, with translateY(-2px).

shadows.name: accent-glow
shadows.purpose: The primary button and active chip. The one place a coloured shadow is allowed, because it is tinted to the accent itself.

shadows.name: stack-card
shadows.purpose: Project stack cards. The most pronounced shadow in the system, reserved for that one component.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Masthead wipe and default state transitions.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Scroll reveals and the wordmark entrance.

motion.name: ease-draw
motion.purpose: The yield curve draw and its lead dot, which share one curve so they read as a single gesture.

motion.name: ease-fold
motion.purpose: The contact band folding up into place.

motion.name: duration-curve-draw
motion.purpose: One full curve draw. Replays every 5s while idle.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one primary action per view. Raspberry fill with an accent-tinted glow.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-family: var(--font-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 500; padding: 11px 20px; border-radius: var(--radius, 12px); border: 1px solid var(--accent, #B23A63); background: var(--accent, #B23A63); color: #fff; text-decoration: none; box-shadow: 0 2px 8px rgba(178,58,99,0.22); transition: transform 120ms ease, box-shadow 120ms ease, background 120ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-deep, #7A2246); box-shadow: 0 6px 16px rgba(178,58,99,0.28); transform: translateY(-1px); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-deep, #7A2246); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: The header's Get in touch action, and the standard secondary call to action. Fills on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; font-family: var(--font-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: var(--radius-xs, 6px); border: 1px solid var(--accent, #B23A63); background: transparent; color: var(--accent, #B23A63); text-decoration: none; transition: background 160ms ease, color 160ms ease; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { background: var(--accent, #B23A63); color: var(--surface, #FFF7F9); } .ds-btn-outline:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-deep, #7A2246); outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Disabled Button
components.description: The reply button before anything is typed. A flat tint rather than a faded fill, so the label stays legible at 6.8:1.
components.css: .ds-btn-disabled { padding: 10px 18px; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius-xs, 6px); background: var(--tint, #F5EBEA); color: var(--ink-72, rgba(25,19,22,0.72)); font-family: var(--font-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 500; cursor: default; }

components.name: Category Chip
components.description: Archive filters. Real links, so a filtered view stays shareable. Active inverts to a soft raspberry fill.
components.html: AllRates & MacroCredit
components.css: .ds-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline; padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: var(--radius-pill, 999px); font-family: var(--font-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 500; white-space: nowrap; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #EADFDD); background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #191316); text-decoration: none; transition: border-color 160ms ease, background 160ms ease, color 160ms ease; } .ds-chip:hover { border-color: var(--ink-45, rgba(25,19,22,0.45)); } .ds-chip-active { border-color: var(--accent, #B23A63); background: var(--accent-soft, #F7ECEF); color: var(--accent, #B23A63); }

components.name: Department Label
components.description: The signature gesture. Mono small-caps raspberry on a raspberry hairline, wherever a section opens.
components.css: .ds-eyebrow { display: block; padding-bottom: 10px; margin-bottom: 14px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--accent, #B23A63); font-family: var(--font-mono), ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent, #B23A63); }

components.name: Archive Row
components.description: One note in the archive: mono date, serif title and deck, mono read time. Three type voices doing their separate jobs in one row.
components.html: 19 Aug 2026Rates & MacroThe Stem Beneath the FlowerThe long end has been supported for two decades. As that support fades, markets are discovering what it costs to keep the flower standing.5 min
components.css: .ds-row { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 118px minmax(0,1fr) 90px; gap: 28px; align-items: baseline; padding: 28px 8px 28px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule, #EADFDD); color: var(--ink, #191316); text-decoration: none; transition: color 160ms ease, background 160ms ease; } .ds-row:hover { background: var(--surface, #FFF7F9); color: var(--accent, #B23A63); } .ds-row-date, .ds-row-read { font-family: var(--font-mono), ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 11.5px; color: var(--ink-60, rgba(25,19,22,0.6)); } .ds-row-read { text-align: right; } .ds-row-cat { display: block; font-family: var(--font-mono), ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 10.5px; letter-spacing: 0.14em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--accent-deep, #7A2246); } .ds-row-title { display: block; font-family: var(--font-serif), Georgia, serif; font-size: 26px; line-height: 1.2; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.019em; margin-top: 8px; } .ds-row-deck { display: block; font-family: var(--font-serif), Georgia, serif; font-size: 17px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--ink-60, rgba(25,19,22,0.6)); margin-top: 8px; }

components.name: Reply Field
components.description: Borderless fields inside one bordered form, so focus lands on the group rather than on each field.
components.css: .ds-form { padding: 18px; border: 1px solid var(--rule, #EADFDD); border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 9px); background: var(--bg, #FCFAF9); } .ds-form:focus-within { border-color: var(--ink-45, rgba(25,19,22,0.45)); } .ds-input-name, .ds-input-text { width: 100%; border: none; background: transparent; color: var(--ink, #191316); outline: none; padding: 6px 2px; } .ds-input-name { font-family: var(--font-sans), system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; } .ds-input-text { font-family: var(--font-serif), Georgia, serif; font-size: 17px; line-height: 1.6; resize: vertical; padding: 8px 2px; } .ds-input-name::placeholder, .ds-input-text::placeholder { color: var(--ink-60, rgba(25,19,22,0.6)); } .ds-divider { height: 1px; background: var(--rule, #EADFDD); margin: 8px 0 4px; }

components.name: Brand Disc
components.description: A flat ink circle carrying bp in the serif. Solid, unlit, no gradient and no rim. It reads as a printer's mark.
components.css: .ds-disc { display: grid; place-items: center; width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--ink, #191316); color: var(--bg, #FCFAF9); font-family: var(--font-serif), Georgia, serif; font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -0.5px; }

narrative.overview:
The Basis Point reads like an analyst's desk note, not a marketing site: a raspberry masthead rule at the very top (the same publication grammar move as the Economist's red bar or the FT's salmon strip), mono small-caps department labels, and long-form serif body copy set to be read closely rather than skimmed. Density is editorial, with generous line-height, real paragraphs and a right rail for supporting context. Never dashboard-dense, never marketing-sparse.

The paper is warm. Blush rather than cool grey is the single decision that most changes the site's temperature: it reads as a printed page rather than an interface, and it lets one saturated colour do all the signalling without ever feeling clinical.

This system explicitly rejects the fintech-SaaS look: no glossy dashboards, no gradient hero sections, no hero-metric templates, no stock trading-floor photography, no numbered-section scaffolding that reads as generated. Confidence comes from restraint and specificity. The writing and the yield curve carry the page, not visual decoration.
keyCharacteristics: One working accent colour (raspberry) used sparingly, with plum as its hover and depth partner
Three type voices with strict jobs: serif reads, sans navigates, mono counts
Publication grammar: masthead rule, section hairlines, mono department labels
Warm blush paper throughout; white is reserved for genuinely raised surfaces
Flat by default; the only shadows are soft ambient lifts on interactive cards and popovers, never structural

rules.name: The One Working Color Rule
rules.body: Raspberry is the only saturated colour on any given screen. Its rarity, a hairline here, a label there, one primary button, is what makes it read as considered rather than decorative. Plum is not an exception to this rule; it is raspberry's own darker state.

rules.name: The Legible Ink Rule
rules.body: --ink-60 is the lightest ink the system may set text in, at 4.7:1. --ink-45 is decoration only: it measures 2.96:1 on blush and fails WCAG AA, so it is for hairlines, borders and list-marker glyphs and never for words.

rules.name: The Three-Voice Rule
rules.body: Serif reads, sans navigates, mono counts. If a piece of text is meant to be read as prose, it is serif. If it is a control or a piece of wayfinding, it is sans. If it is a date, a duration, a tenor, a basis-point figure or a department label, it is mono. Never mix two voices mid-sentence.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Measurable Rule
rules.body: Mono is not a decorative technical texture to sprinkle on headings. It earns its place only where the content is genuinely a label or a quantity. A serif heading never becomes mono for effect.

rules.name: The Hairline-Before-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Reach for a 1px hairline border before reaching for a shadow. Shadows are earned by interaction state, not applied at rest.

rules.name: The Focus Is Not Optional Rule
rules.body: Every focusable control carries one ring: 2px solid raspberry at 2px offset, on :focus-visible. The rule is written unlayered so no component rule can suppress it. If you are reaching for outline: none, that rule is what you are fighting: give the element a better indicator rather than removing the one it has. On the contact band the ring turns to ink with a paper halo, because that backdrop is a photograph.

dos: Do keep raspberry to hairlines, labels, links, and the primary button. One working colour, used sparingly.
Do set long-form reading copy in the serif family at 19.5px/1.78, capped at 65 to 75ch.
Do reach for a 1px hairline border before a shadow; let shadows respond to interaction rather than sitting at rest.
Do keep the 3px raspberry masthead rule unique to the very top of the page.
Do set every date, read time, tenor and basis-point figure in mono.
Do keep the contact band's photograph under its wash; the wash is not optional.
donts: Don't use border-left/border-right as a coloured accent stripe on cards or list items. The masthead rule is the site's one sanctioned stripe at the top, and the pull-quote's left rule is the one sanctioned stripe in body copy. Nothing else.
Don't use gradient text or background-clip: text gradients anywhere, and never put a gradient on the brand disc.
Don't build glossy fintech-dashboard components: no gradient hero sections, no hero-metric templates, no stock trading-floor imagery.

Don't scatter mono uppercase labels as reflexive scaffolding. Mono labels are department markers and quantities, so one sits above an editorial break or beside a measurement, and never above every div for texture.
Don't add numbered section markers (01/02/03) as decoration. The About page's photo counter is a real index of a real set, and is the only exception.
Don't mix two type voices within the same piece of running text.
Don't reintroduce a second accent colour. The old system reserved a warm tan that was never placed in the UI in three months; the lesson is that this palette does not need one.
Don't set text in --ink-45. It fails WCAG AA and PRODUCT.md commits to AA.
Don't set text in --ink-45. It measures 2.96:1 and PRODUCT.md commits to WCAG AA. --ink-60 is the lightest ink any text may use.
Don't write outline: none. If a control needs a different focus treatment, give it a better one; never leave it with none.
Don't make a hit target smaller than it looks. The About carousel's dots read as 2px bars but are 14px controls, with the background clipped to the content box.
